title: Aphorism § 233
text:
§ 233



 The typical intermittent disease are those where a morbid state of
          unvarying character returns at a tolerably fixed period, while the patient is apparently
          in good health, and takes its departure at an equally fixed period; this is observed in
          those apparently non-febrile morbid states that come and go in a periodical manner (at
          certain times), as well as in those of a febrile character, to wit, the numerous varieties
          of intermittent fevers.
